description: Generates four voices of euclidean rhythm as one MPX note stream, each voice with its own pattern, clock division and wandering level

params.text: Sets how many steps that voice's pattern is long, 1 to 32
Sets how many of that voice's steps sound, 0 to 32, spread as evenly through the pattern as they can be
Rotates that voice's pattern by a number of steps, 0 to 31, without changing which steps sound relative to each other
Sets how fast that voice is clocked relative to the incoming beat: every beat, half speed, a third or a quarter
Sets the level the voices wander around, 0 to 100%
Sets how far the level is allowed to wander from that setting, 0 to 100%
Sets the length of a note, 0.01 to 4 seconds, exponential so the short end has most of the travel
Sets how strongly a note's length follows its level, 0 to 100%, so louder notes can also be longer
Sets how fast the wandering moves, a quarter to sixteen beats per cycle
Sets how many beats pass before the wandering repeats itself, 1 to 64
Sets the tempo when no clock is patched, 30 to 300 beats per minute

inputs.text: Advances the patterns; patching anything here overrides the tempo knob
Returns every voice to the start of its pattern

outputs.text: Carries all four voices on as one MPX stream

notes: mpx OUT carries a note stream, not a voltage; patch it to another DreamerMPX module's mpx IN, or to mpxOut where ordinary voltages are wanted
a cable between two MPX jacks turns pink once it has taken; a cable from an MPX jack to anything else keeps its ordinary colour and carries nothing
an MPX cable carries a note stream rather than a voltage and goes to an MPX input; mpxOut turns a stream back into gates and pitch for the wider rack
